name: Mohammed bin Salman Al Saud
role: Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Saudi Arabia (crown prince since 2017, prime minister since 2022); de facto ruler
summary: Mohammed bin Salman leads Saudi Arabia as an authoritarian monarchy while driving economic diversification through Vision 2030, privatisation and the Public Investment Fund. He has cut the powers of the religious police and clerics, ended the driving ban and loosened guardianship, while keeping Islam as the constitutional basis and jailing critics. In foreign policy he is hostile to Iran, close to the US, open to Israeli normalisation tied to a Palestinian state, and says Saudi Arabia would seek nuclear weapons if Iran did.

sources.title: What the Saudi crown prince's latest interview says about the future of Saudi Arabia (Graeme Wood on his Atlantic interview, March 2022)
sources.author: NPR
sources.usedFor: Second-hand account of what he told The Atlantic about dissent and Khashoggi; the Atlantic text itself was unreachable.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In 2016 he said the aim is to move government health assets into a holding company and to persuade citizens that insurance-based care is better and faster than free state care; Vision 2030 corporatises public health providers with privatisation in view, while promising support for the most vulnerable.

public-ownership.rationale: He is selling shares in Aramco and moving water, energy and other services to private operators, but said Aramco and Sabic stay majority-owned by the state fund, so the evidence is mixed.

property-fundamental.rationale: He ordered the 2017 detention of princes and businessmen and said over $35 billion in assets and cash had been transferred to the state through settlements; the government presents these as recovery of corrupt gains, while critics describe coercion.

empower-police-military.rationale: As defence minister and ruler he has overseen very large military spending, and Vision 2030 promises the army the best possible equipment.

traditional-family.rationale: Vision 2030 states that families are the key building block of society, protecting it from social breakdown, and names Islamic values and extended family ties as defining Saudi traits.

more-religion-public.rationale: He said Saudi Arabia was not like this before 1979 and that the country is returning to a moderate Islam, and he limited the religious police and opened cinemas and concerts.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Vision 2030 commits to strengthen, preserve and highlight national identity, uphold Arabic and restore heritage sites.

gradual-change.rationale: He asked the world for time on women's rights, citing the slow US path to women's suffrage, and said change comes without civil war, yet his own reforms have been rapid and top-down.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Vision 2030 seeks to attract talent and improve visas, residency and living conditions for qualified non-Saudis, while also aiming to raise Saudi employment.

limit-growth.rationale: Vision 2030 and his interviews set growth as a goal (a larger economy, more jobs, higher non-oil revenue); he told Fox he would keep investing in sport if it adds a point or more to GDP.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: In 2021 he announced net zero by 2060 and a cut of 278 Mt a year by 2030, but through a circular carbon economy that keeps oil's role, and in 2018 he said electric vehicles pose no risk to oil.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He restructured the Public Investment Fund to steer capital into chosen sectors (renewables, industry, real estate, a transformed Aramco) and Vision 2030 names the strategic sectors and localisation targets the state will pursue.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He took the position of heir by replacing Muhammad bin Nayef in 2017 and has described the ruler as the head of the Islamic establishment (wali al-amr); his conduct shows he treats hereditary monarchy as legitimate.

separate-church-state.rationale: Vision 2030 describes Islam as the constitution and Islamic principles as the driving force of the state, though he has cut clerical powers within that framework.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Vision 2030 calls for a country with Islam as its constitution, and he said reforms go forward without leaving Saudi laws based on religion.

military-superiority.rationale: Vision 2030 commits to giving the army the best possible machinery and to build domestic defence capacity, and he calls Iran a threat that must be deterred firmly.

restore-past-order.rationale: He frames reform as a return to the Saudi Arabia of before 1979, but pairs it with a technology-driven future; no source weighs restoration against progress.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In 2018 he reportedly said Jewish people have a right to a homeland in peace; he later said normalisation moves closer with Palestinian needs met.

national-self-determination.rationale: He has said Saudi Arabia will not normalise relations with Israel without a Palestinian state with East Jerusalem as capital, and told Fox any deal must give Palestinians what they need.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: He said women can work in any sector, ended the driving ban, and said the guardianship rules date from 1979 and could be changed; guardianship rules in personal status remain.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He has said Saudi Arabia keeps spare oil capacity and will supply the market as needed, and expects oil demand to keep rising for some years; this sits alongside diversification and renewables targets.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He launched the anti-corruption campaign that detained princes and ministers in 2017, saying no one would be spared, and said over $35 billion was recovered; this treats elite corruption as real.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: On Khashoggi he said he took responsibility as leader, that those involved were prosecuted and jailed, and that security rules were reformed, while denying he ordered the killing; the answer is low as the proceedings were closed and contested.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Vision 2030 commits to complete the GCC common market, unifying customs, economic and legal policies.

clerical-rule.rationale: He curtailed the religious police, told clerics the ruler holds authority over the Islamic establishment, and said no one is infallible and fatwas must reflect time and place.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He described Saudi Arabia as the main ally of the US in the Middle East and the US partnership as huge, which runs against ending alliances; there is no statement on troop withdrawal.

death-penalty.rationale: No stated position of his own found; Saudi Arabia's retention of capital punishment is the state's record, not his statement.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: He told Fox in 2023 that if Iran gets a nuclear weapon, Saudi Arabia must get one for security and to balance power; he does not say it would drop its US ties.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He restricted the religious police, reportedly pressed clerics to back government positions, and described the ruler as head of the Islamic establishment; no sources opened address clergy property.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Vision 2030 promises to extend non-Saudis' ability to own real estate in certain areas, which rejects a blanket ban, though ownership stays limited.

religious-nation.rationale: Vision 2030 names Islamic faith and national unity as what make the nation exceptional, yet he also says the country is open to all religions.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Vision 2030 sets out delivery of health, education, housing and municipal services through public corporations, private firms and the non-profit sector, with competition among providers and citizen choice of provider.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Activists, clerics and critics were jailed under his rule; he said about 1,500 people were arrested in three years, that most cases have nothing to do with speech, and that people are free to dissent if professional.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: He campaigns against extremist ideologies and said extremists distort Islam; he has also fought Islamist movements that reject rulers.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He is a major arms buyer and plans to produce half of military equipment needs at home.

dynastic-succession.rationale: He became crown prince on his father's decision in 2017, set aside a rival heir, and took the premiership from his father in 2022; no opened source records his words on succession itself.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: He said there are no fixed schools of thought, that no one is infallible and that fatwas depend on time and place, and he said guardianship rules were being reviewed with senior scholars to see what is Islamic.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Vision 2030 aims to raise the non-profit sector from under 1% to 5% of GDP and give it a larger role in health, education and housing, though it does not say charities outperform state programmes.

local-essentials-public.rationale: He said in 2018 that over twenty services would be privatised in 2019, most of them in water, agriculture and energy, and Vision 2030 corporatises hospitals for later privatisation.

women-suffrage.rationale: He pointed to women voting and winning seats in the 2015 municipal elections and said women can work in any sector, including politics, adding that more time is needed; Saudi Arabia still has no national elections.

close-ties-china.rationale: He named China as a target market for Aramco and hosted Xi Jinping in 2022 to raise ties to a comprehensive strategic partnership, while saying the US partnership is huge and calling Saudi Arabia America's main regional ally.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: His government introduced VAT and excise taxes on sugary drinks and energy drinks and he said in 2018 that this tax reform was done.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Vision 2030 says subsidies for fuel, food, water and electricity will be redirected towards those in need rather than provided to all.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Vision 2030 says its technology-led plan will be achieved by adhering closely to Islamic principles, Arab values and national traditions, and in 2017 he paired a return to the past with a technology-driven future.

national-resource-control.rationale: He said Aramco and Sabic remain majority-owned by the state fund with only a small share listed, and Vision 2030 commits to continue localising the oil and gas sector.

notes: The Atlantic (2018, 2022), 60 Minutes 2018, Al Arabiya 2021 and Fox full broadcast texts were unreachable or paywalled, so answers rely on the sources listed. Positions on Israel have shifted: support for a Jewish homeland in 2018, closeness to normalisation in 2023, then insistence on a Palestinian state in 2024. Khashoggi: he accepted responsibility as leader but denied ordering the killing; US intelligence assessed otherwise.
